# StrategySphere — Technical Requirements

**Status: as-built, v3.2.0.** Generated by reading the models, the router table
and the migrations, not from memory. 45 route operations, 13 tables, 4
migrations, 515 tests, 9,432 lines of backend and 5,009 of frontend.

---

## Architecture

```
React 18 + TS (Vite)          nginx / vite dev proxy          FastAPI
  one component per stage  ──────  /api  ────────────────  routers (HTTP only)
  no business logic                                              │
                                                                 ▼
                                                          services/  ← the product
                                                     pure functions over dicts;
                                                     no DB, no network, no FastAPI
                                                                 │
                            ┌────────────────────────────────────┼───────────────┐
                            ▼                                    ▼               ▼
                    PostgreSQL 16 / SQLite              services/edgar/     LLM endpoint 
                    13 tables, Alembic                 the only outbound    narration only,
                    JSON + UUID dialect variants       caller; data.sec.gov  optional
```

**Layer rule.** No *engine* module in `services/` imports `app.db`, `app.models`
or `fastapi`, which is what makes every engine testable without a database or a
network. Exactly two modules in that package cross the line, both deliberately:
`analysis_pipeline.py`, which is the seam between the ORM and the engines, and
`jobs.py`, whose source of truth is a `jobs` row.

| Layer | Responsibility | Must not |
|---|---|---|
| `frontend/src` | Render stored results, collect inputs | Compute any displayed figure |
| `app/routers` | Validate, call a service, persist, shape the response | Hold business logic |
| `app/services` | All arithmetic, all framework logic | Touch the DB or the network |
| `app/services/edgar` | Outbound HTTP, caching, rate limiting | Be called from a request path synchronously |
| `app/db` | Session, the read layer, cursor pagination | Interpret a result |
| `app/models` | Table definitions | Contain methods that compute |
| `app/framework.py` | Validate the parameter set, compute its digest | Know what any parameter means |

---

## Database

PostgreSQL 16 in Docker; SQLite for tests and local runs. `JsonBlob` is a
dialect variant (JSONB on PostgreSQL, JSON on SQLite) and UUIDs likewise, which
is why the API tests exercise the real app with no database container in CI.

### Entities

| Table | Rows mean | Key columns |
|---|---|---|
| `companies` | One company **as reported for one period** | `entity_key`, `period_label`, `period_end`, `financial_data`, `market_data`, `feature_scores`, `qualitative_inputs`, `uncertainty_inputs` |
| `competitors` | The peer set a company is benchmarked against | `company_id`, `price_point`, `market_share_pct`, `feature_scores`, `financial_data` |
| `swot_analyses` | One scoring run | `strengths`/`weaknesses`/`opportunities`/`threats` (JSON), `calculation_basis` |
| `market_attractiveness` | One matrix placement | four axis scores, `overall_attractiveness_score`, `competitive_strength_score`, `quadrant`, `borderline` |
| `pricing_recommendations` | One pricing run | `cost_base`, `competitor_avg_price`, `target_margin_pct`, `margin_basis` |
| `strategy_reports` | One narration | narrative JSON, which narrator produced it, dropped-factor count |
| `porters_analyses` | One Five Forces run | per-force score + source tag, composite, coverage |
| `scenarios` | A named override set | `overrides` (JSON), diff vs baseline |
| `uncertainty_analyses` | One Monte-Carlo run | quadrant probabilities, CIs, `entropy_bits`, stability band |
| `portfolios` | A set of units sharing one budget | `budget` |
| `portfolio_members` | One unit's ask | `capital_requested`, `capital_floor`, `revenue` |
| `allocation_runs` | One allocation | `allocations`, `unfunded`, `marginal_unit`, `harvest_contribution` |
| `jobs` | A background task; the row is the source of truth | `kind`, `state`, `progress`, `heartbeat_at`, `cancel_requested`, `request_id` |

### Relationships

`companies` 1—N everything analytical, all `ON DELETE CASCADE`.
`market_attractiveness.swot_analysis_id` is `ON DELETE SET NULL` — a placement
records which SWOT run fed it, but outliving that run is not an error.
`portfolio_members` is the join between `portfolios` and `companies`.

### Indexes

| Index | Why it exists |
|---|---|
| `(company_id, <ts> DESC)` on every result table | The read layer fetches the latest row with `ORDER BY … LIMIT 1`; without this it is a scan |
| `ix_companies_created_id (created_at, id)` | The keyset pagination tuple |
| `ix_companies_entity_period (entity_key, period_end)` | Timeline assembly |
| `ix_jobs_state_heartbeat (state, heartbeat_at)` | The orphan reaper's query |
| `ix_allocation_runs_portfolio_created` | Latest allocation per portfolio |

### Constraints

Enforced in Pydantic schemas rather than only in the database, so a bad value is
rejected with a field path before it reaches SQL. Bounds are deliberate: they
are why a typo cannot produce a confident wrong number.

## APIs

45 operations. Full request/response shapes are in the generated OpenAPI at
`/docs`; this is the map.

### Companies

| Method | Route | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `GET` | `/companies` | Keyset paginated (`limit`, `cursor`), filters `industry`, `q`, optional `with_total` |
| `POST` | `/companies` | `201` |
| `GET`/`DELETE` | `/companies/{id}` | |
| `GET`/`POST` | `/companies/{id}/competitors` | |

### Analysis stages

Every stage is `POST` to run, `GET` to read the latest.

`/companies/{id}/swot-analysis` · `/market-attractiveness` ·
`/pricing-recommendation` · `/porters-analysis` · `/uncertainty` ·
`/generate-strategy-report` (POST) and `/strategy-report` (GET) ·
`/sensitivity` (GET only — derived from the stored matrix row) ·
`/scenarios` (GET/POST, plus `DELETE /scenarios/{scenario_id}`)

### Portfolio, timeline, validation, ops

| Method | Route | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `GET`/`POST` | `/portfolios`, `GET`/`DELETE /portfolios/{id}` | |
| `POST` | `/portfolios/{id}/allocate` | `409 BUDGET_INFEASIBLE` if floors exceed budget |
| `GET` | `/portfolios/{id}/allocations` | |
| `GET` | `/entities`, `/entities/{key}/timeline` | |
| `POST` | `/validation/backtest`, `/validation/panels` | Panel build is a job |
| `POST` | `/benchmarks/build` | `202` + `Location`; `out` restricted to relative paths under `data/` |
| `GET` | `/benchmarks/provenance` | Where the live table came from |
| `GET` | `/jobs`, `/jobs/{id}` (sets `Retry-After: 2`), `POST /jobs/{id}/cancel` | |
| `GET` | `/framework` | The active parameter set, its digest, its source, and which fields the environment overrode |
| `GET` | `/methodology` | Serves an ETag; answers a matching request with `304` |
| `GET` | `/health`, `/ready`, `/metrics` | `/metrics` is `include_in_schema=False` |

### Error contract

RFC 9457 `problem+json` for every failure, including the ones FastAPI raises
itself, so there is one shape to parse. The prose `detail` is preserved for
backwards compatibility.

```json
{ "type": "…/stage-order", "title": "Pipeline stage out of order",
  "status": 409, "code": "STAGE_ORDER", "detail": "…",
  "request_id": "…" }
```

Closed set of codes: `NOT_FOUND` 404 · `STAGE_ORDER` 409 ·
`INSUFFICIENT_INPUT` 422 · `INVALID_INPUT` 422 · `CONFLICT` 409 ·
`BUDGET_INFEASIBLE` 409 · `UPSTREAM_UNAVAILABLE` 502 · `NOT_CONFIGURED` 501 ·
`JOB_CONFLICT` 409 · `RATE_LIMITED` 429 · `INTERNAL` 500.

### Auth

**None.** No authentication, no authorization, no tenancy. Deliberate: this is a
single-analyst tool and adding auth would imply a trust boundary that does not
exist. **Consequence: do not expose this API to the public internet as-is.**
Anyone who can reach it can read and delete every company.

---

## Security

| Concern | Position |
|---|---|
| Authentication | None. See above. Bind to localhost or put it behind something. |
| Input validation | Pydantic v2 at the boundary with explicit bounds on every numeric field |
| Path traversal | Both job endpoints that accept an `out` path (`/benchmarks/build`, `/validation/panels`) reject absolute paths, `..` segments, and anything outside `data/`. The shared validator is `_contained_in_data` in `app/schemas` |
| SSRF | The EDGAR client refuses any host outside `data.sec.gov` / `www.sec.gov` |
| Outbound rate | Token bucket, 5 req/s default under the published 10, `burst` 1, thread-safe |
| Secrets | `LLM_API_KEY` and `EDGAR_USER_AGENT` from env only. `.env` is gitignored and no secret is committed |
| Contact disclosure | `EDGAR_USER_AGENT` must contain a contact address — SEC requires it. It is a real email, so it stays in env and never in the repo |
| Logs | JSON, with a request id per line. Payloads are not logged |
| CORS | Explicit origin allowlist, default `localhost:5173,localhost:3000` |
| SQL injection | No raw SQL on a request path; the read layer is parameterized ORM |
| DoS | No request rate limiting. Another reason not to expose it publicly |

## Deployment

**Hosting.** `docker compose up --build` — PostgreSQL 16 Alpine, backend,
frontend behind nginx. Bare-metal instructions in [running.md](running.md).

**Build.** Backend `pip install -r requirements-dev.txt`; frontend
`tsc -b && vite build`. Migrations are explicit: `alembic upgrade head`. The app
does not create tables.

**Environment variables.** Full list in `backend/app/config.py`; the ones that
matter:

| Variable | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `DATABASE_URL` | PostgreSQL localhost | SQLite works for everything |
| `LLM_BASE_URL` / `LLM_MODEL` | *(empty)* | Any OpenAI-compatible endpoint, hosted or local. Empty means template fallback, not failure |
| `LLM_API_KEY` | *(empty)* | Sent as a bearer token; optional for local servers |
| `EDGAR_USER_AGENT` | *(empty, required)* | No default. SEC requires a contact address |
| `EDGAR_REQUESTS_PER_SECOND` | `5.0` | Published ceiling is 10 |
| `EDGAR_OFFLINE` | `false` | Cache-only; fails loudly rather than fetching |
| `EDGAR_MIN_SECTOR_N` | `20` | Below this a sector is withheld |
| `INDUSTRY_BENCHMARKS_PATH` | *(empty)* | Empty falls back to peer-set medians only |
| `UNCERTAINTY_SEED` | `20260921` | Changing it changes the draws |
| `VALIDATION_RANDOM_SEED` | `20260908` | The published permutation tests use this |
| `API_PROXY_TARGET` | `http://localhost:8000` | Frontend dev proxy only |

Every threshold in the framework is a parameter, not a literal. The 43 that can
change a computed figure live in **`data/framework.json`**, not in the
environment: quadrant thresholds, axis weights, the neutral band and its impact
buckets, HHI bands, Porter coverage minimums, the uncertainty seed and draw
count, the harvest contribution rate.

The file is validated as a set rather than one field at a time — axis weights
must sum to 1.0, thresholds must be ordered, the borderline margin cannot be
wide enough to swallow the middle quadrant — and carries a **digest** over the
parameter values, stamped into every stored result. A verdict therefore records
the parameterisation that produced it, and `GET /framework` maps a digest back
to a file.

Precedence is deliberate: an environment variable overrides the file, because an
operator setting one at run time is a deliberate act. Overridden fields are
listed in `env_overrides` on every stamp, so an override cannot hide. A missing
file degrades to the code defaults, because the system must still produce
complete output; an *invalid* file refuses to start, because a wrong parameter
set computes quietly, which is worse than not computing.

**Monitoring.** `/metrics` in Prometheus text format, labelled by route template
so cardinality stays bounded. `/health` is liveness, `/ready` checks the
database. Request ids flow from the inbound `X-Request-ID` header through every
log line and into every error body.

**CI.** Python 3.10 and 3.12. Beyond `pytest`: EDGAR fixtures are regenerated and
diffed, the OpenAPI schema must generate, migrations round-trip, the read-layer
benchmark runs so an N+1 cannot creep back, and a check asserts no test opens a
socket.

---

## Risks

| Risk | Severity | State |
|---|---|---|
| No auth on a mutating API | High if exposed | Documented; mitigation is deployment topology |
| Backtest look-ahead bias | High | Published in `validation_results.md`; fix is V4 |
| Results do not record which benchmark table scored them | Medium | **Half closed.** Every result now carries `calculation_basis.framework` — the digest of the parameter set that produced it. The benchmark *table* is still unversioned, so a result records its thresholds but not which sector medians it compared against. That half is V4 |
| `jobs` is single-process; two API processes both reap | Medium | Fine for the intended single-process deployment, wrong under a replica set |
| EDGAR tag drift breaks resolution | Medium | Ordered candidate tags + coverage published per metric + CI fixture diff |
| No request rate limiting | Low locally | `RATE_LIMITED` exists in the taxonomy but nothing emits it yet |
| An `out` path escaping `data/` | **Was high** | Found by writing this document: `PanelBuildRequest` shipped without the containment validator `BenchmarkBuildRequest` had, so `POST /validation/panels` could name any writable path. Validator now shared, with a parameterized regression test over both routes |

### The class of bug this architecture has actually produced

Worth stating, because it shapes where to look next: the two worst defects found
in V3 were a **fixture that agreed with the code and both disagreed with
reality** (balance-sheet concepts are instantaneous, `CY2024` is a 404) and a
**rate limiter that allowed twice its configured rate** because `capacity ==
rate`. Neither was reachable by unit test. Both were found by running the thing
against the real API and measuring. Full list in
[architecture.md](architecture.md).
